title: No split for zero input
statement: For all $C,c\in\mathbb{N}$, the value $\mathrm{split}_{C,c}(0)$ is undefined; equivalently, there is no $n\in\{0\}$ such that $n+(C+1)(n+1)^c=0$.
replaced:
For $C, c, m \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\mathrm{split}_{C,c}(m)$ be the least
$n \le m$ with $n + (C+1)(n+1)^c = m$, and undefined if there is none. Then for
all $C, c \in \mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{split}_{C,c}(0)$ is undefined.
